references.text: The Lord came down on Mount Sinai and called Moses up to the top of the mountain, an earlier event where Moses was summoned to the mountain to meet God.
Moses receives the two tablets of the testimony, stone tablets written by the finger of God, fulfilling the promise of the stone tablets in 24:12.
Describes the stone tablets that were written by God on both sides, the tablets Moses received on the mountain.
God commands Moses to carve out new stone tablets after the first ones were broken and to go up the mountain again.
Moses recounts that the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on two stone tablets and gave them to him.
Moses retells how he went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets of the covenant that the Lord had made with Israel.
Moses describes the new stone tablets and how they were placed in the ark, fulfilling God's promise to give the law on stone tablets.
Confirms that there was nothing in the ark except the two stone tablets that Moses laid there at Horeb.
Paul contrasts stone tablets with tablets of fleshly hearts, referring to the tables of the law given to Moses.
Refers to Moses being warned when he was to build the tabernacle and receiving instructions on the mountain.
Mentions the tablets of the covenant that were kept in the ark, the tablets Moses received from God.
Both verses describe God's instruction to make new stone tablets as a replacement for the broken ones, together forming a complete account of the restoration of the covenant.
The verses illuminate each other by showing two sides of the same matter: God's original inscription on the tablets and Moses' writing as confirmation of the covenant.
Deuteronomy 10:1 confirms and expands upon the original instruction from Exodus 24:12 to go up the mountain to receive new tablets.
The verse describes the concrete fulfillment of God's command to carve out new tablets and go up the mountain, first given in 24:12.
The verse confirms the divine origin of the tablets mentioned in Exodus 24:12 by emphasizing that they were written with God's finger.
